panel_B.definition: wrench_norm = |ee_force| in newtons (run_probes_xr1.wrench_norm_of), the same target that analysis/run_probes_xr1.py already probes
panel_B.question: does the model track the IMMEDIATE CONTACT CONSEQUENCE (the force it is feeling) even where it fails to track the LATENT PROPERTY (the mass)?
lines: XR1 action module (DiT L28, flow4 state-block)
panel_B.physics_ceiling_excluded: Panel B deliberately has NO physics-ceiling line: its features are the wrist F/T sensor itself, so decoding |F| from it would be circular (reading the target off the instrument that defines it), not a ceiling.
panel_B.shared_with_panel_A: identical bins, identical rows, identical GroupKFold(5) fold partition and identical per-fold SVD factors -- panel A and panel B are literally the same fits scored against two different labels
panel_B.reading: Panel B deliberately has NO physics-ceiling line: its features are the wrist F/T sensor itself, so decoding |F| from it would be circular (reading the target off the instrument that defines it), not a ceiling. XR1 action module (DiT L28, flow4 state-block): |F| selectivity peaks +0.603 (R² 0.561, shuffled std 0.024, rank 0.587) in [-3.2,-1.6) s (n=200) — BEATS its own mass peak (+0.356 @ +4.0 s). XR1 wrist-camera tokens (VLM L21): |F| selectivity peaks +0.611 (R² 0.546, shuffled std 0.028, rank 0.570) in [-3.2,-1.6) s (n=200) — BEATS its own mass peak (+0.175 @ +4.0 s). XR1 proprioception (state_embed): |F| selectivity peaks +0.380 (R² 0.356, shuffled std 0.018, rank 0.524) in [-3.2,-1.6) s (n=200) — BEATS its own mass peak (+0.017 @ +0.8 s). commanded-vs-achieved deficit (k=8 window): |F| selectivity peaks +0.470 (R² 0.436, shuffled std 0.021, rank 0.524) in [-3.2,-1.6) s (n=200) — BEATS its own mass peak (+0.103 @ +2.4 s).

camera_pixel_line.label: camera pixels — OUR 96×96 reader (not model vision)
camera_pixel_line.what_it_is: OUR reader, not the model's vision: vision_certificate.py's ridge-on-PCA reader over 96x96 GRAYSCALE stored frames in XR1's own visual format (4 frames at stride 2 x 3 cameras, its own 0.95 centre crop), i.e. the amendment-C 'ridge_pca' cell re-cut into these bins
camera_pixel_line.leakage_rule: PCA(512) fitted on the TRAIN rows WITHIN EACH FOLD only (amendment C Section 2) -- an all-rows PCA would carry held-out structure into the representation and could invent a positive; vision_certificate.pca_fold_factors is imported, not re-implemented
camera_pixel_line.row_scope: only rows whose whole stored 4-frame window exists. render_frames.frame_steps_needed stored the precontact steps and the carry windows ONLY, so captured rows inside the grasp transition or after the place have no frames. Substituting a neighbouring frame would corrupt the format, so those rows are EXCLUDED and the retention rule (>=120 rows, >=15 episodes) is re-applied to the subset; a bin that fails it is dropped for this line only and the line is drawn with a GAP there
camera_pixel_line.matched_comparator: 'XR1 wrist-camera tokens (VLM L21) on the pixel rows [diagnostic]' re-scores VLM L21 on exactly this line's rows and folds, so the instrument asymmetry is not a comparison between two row sets. Recorded in the parquet and here; never plotted
camera_pixel_line.reader_is_a_lower_bound: a reader can miss information, never invent it: this line finding nothing is evidence about THIS reader on THIS 96x96 grayscale reduction, not proof the camera channel lacks mass
camera_pixel_line.reading: Camera-pixel reader (OURS, 96×96 grey, in-fold PCA + ridge — NOT the model's vision): peak selectivity +0.126 (real R² 0.0071, shuffled std 0.0758, rank 0.575) in [+4.8,+6.4) s on n=141 rows, over 6 retained bins. XR1's own wrist-camera TOKENS (VLM L21) peak at +0.175 (real R² 0.1391) in [+3.2,+4.8) s. On EXACTLY the camera reader's rows and folds, VLM L21 still peaks at +0.292 (real R² 0.2527, [+3.2,+4.8) s, n=147), so the gap is not an artifact of the two lines being scored on different row sets. Read this as an INSTRUMENT asymmetry, not a claim that the pixels lack mass: a reader is a lower bound on channel content — it can miss information, never invent it — so our low-resolution reader finding nothing is evidence about THIS reader on THIS 96×96 grayscale reduction, while the model's encoder finding something is evidence the channel carries it.

place_event.definition: first step after lift-off at which the gripper has released (grasped False) AND the object is no longer rising (obj_z[t] <= obj_z[t-1] + 0.0001 m)
place_event.why_not_initial_height: the task places the object on a CABINET SHELF about 0.5 m ABOVE the counter it was picked up from, so obj_z never returns to obj_z[0]: an init_z-relative rule fires in only 17/100 episodes on this corpus, this one in 95/100
place_event.first_place_not_last: 44 of 95 episodes re-close the gripper after their first release, so the detector deliberately returns the FIRST place

config.physics_line: certificates.build_features('raw_ft'): ee_force[3]+ee_torque[3]+derived [|F|,|tau|,F_world[3],F_base[3]], per-episode trailing window k=16 stride 1, z-scored per cell exactly as certificates.certificate_cell does (mixed physical units); activations are NOT z-scored (run_probes_xr1 convention)
config.deficit_line: certificates.build_features('deficit'): commanded_delta[6]+achieved_eef_delta[6], per-episode trailing window k=8 stride 1, z-scored per cell exactly as certificates.certificate_cell does (mixed units: normalized OSC action vs metres) -- the identical builder the 'deficit' certificate uses (carry-mask R^2 0.062, FAIL); this line asks whether that channel's time profile spikes at contact or stays flat, not whether it passes the certificate gate

bin_rule.chosen_for: sample sufficiency, fixed before any curve was computed; NOT tuned on outcomes

protocol.cv: GroupKFold(5) by SEED (identical fold partition for every site within a bin and a row scope; the per-fold SVD factors are shared across both targets too)
protocol.shuffle: group-coherent by EPISODE, per-draw alpha search

figure_caption: EXPLORATORY post-hoc time resolution of the pre-registered carry-phase probe result — no new claim, same rows/targets/discipline at finer time grain. Selectivity = real pooled held-out R² minus mean shuffled R² (5 group-coherent shuffles, each with its own alpha search); band = ±1 shuffled std. GroupKFold(5) by SEED, shuffles group-coherent by EPISODE; identical rows and folds for every line within a panel and a row scope. PANEL A: target mass_log_c (the latent property). PANEL B: target wrench_norm = |F| in newtons (the immediate contact consequence), same bins/rows/folds/shuffles, showing ONLY the three model sites and the deficit channel — the wrist-F/T physics ceiling is deliberately ABSENT there because its features are the force sensor itself, so decoding |F| from it would be circular rather than a ceiling. The sixth panel-A line, 'camera pixels — OUR 96×96 reader (not model vision)', is OUR reader (vision_certificate.py's ridge-on-PCA over 96×96 grayscale frames in XR1's 4-frame stride-2 × 3-camera format, PCA fitted on the TRAIN rows of each fold only) — it is NOT the model's vision, and it is scored only on rows whose stored frame window exists (render_frames kept precontact and carry windows only), so it is retained in [-4.8,-3.2)s, [-3.2,-1.6)s, [-1.6,+0.0)s, [+1.6,+3.2)s, [+3.2,+4.8)s, [+4.8,+6.4)s and absent elsewhere; a row-matched VLM L21 cell on exactly those rows is recorded in the summary json as the fair comparator. Bins 1.6 s (32 steps @20 Hz), span −6.4..+9.6 s, retained only if ≥120 rows and ≥15 episodes (8 retained; dropped: [-6.4,-4.8)s (n=64 < 120 rows); [+8.0,+9.6)s (n=75 < 120 rows)). Median lift-off +0.70 s; median place/release +5.65 s (the third rule — it is why every line decays late in the span). Headline unchanged: peak carry-phase selectivity 0.227 (R² 0.189) at DiT L28, below the 0.3 bar.
figure_note_on_png: EXPLORATORY post-hoc re-cut of the pre-registered carry-phase probe result — no new claim; full method caption in timecurve_summary.json.
peak_vs_pre_registered_headline: The DiT L28 line peaks at selectivity 0.356 (R² 0.341, shuffled std 0.013) in the [+3.2,+4.8) s bin (centre +4.0 s) on n=181 rows, ABOVE the pre-registered phase-bucket value of 0.227 (R² 0.189, carry mask, n=809). Read it as a NOISIER single-bin estimate, NOT a better result: those 181 rows are 8% of the 2,413 captured rows and about 22% the size of the pre-registered 809-row carry cell, and the bin was selected as this line's maximum over 8 bins (a max-over-bins statistic is upward-biased). The study's headline is unchanged and stays below the 0.3 certificate bar.
precontact_reading: Pre-contact bins (3 retained, −4.8..0.0 s): the largest selectivity is +0.089 (camera pixels — OUR 96×96 reader (not model vision), [-4.8,-3.2) s), but the largest REAL pooled held-out R² over all six panel-A lines and all pre-contact bins is only +0.0039 — i.e. no line predicts mass better than the training-fold mean before contact. Those small positive selectivities come from the shuffled control scoring NEGATIVE (shuffled R² ≈ −0.02..−0.05, the usual grouped-CV behaviour when a permuted per-episode label is fit across folds), not from real pre-contact signal. Nothing here qualifies the study's leakage story: the pre-registered guard (mass selectivity < 0.1 at every probed cell on the precontact mask) also still holds at this grain.
panel_b_reading: Panel B deliberately has NO physics-ceiling line: its features are the wrist F/T sensor itself, so decoding |F| from it would be circular (reading the target off the instrument that defines it), not a ceiling. XR1 action module (DiT L28, flow4 state-block): |F| selectivity peaks +0.603 (R² 0.561, shuffled std 0.024, rank 0.587) in [-3.2,-1.6) s (n=200) — BEATS its own mass peak (+0.356 @ +4.0 s). camera_vs_vlm_reading: Camera-pixel reader (OURS, 96×96 grey, in-fold PCA + ridge — NOT the model's vision): peak selectivity +0.126 (real R² 0.0071, shuffled std 0.0758, rank 0.575) in [+4.8,+6.4) s on n=141 rows, over 6 retained bins. XR1's own wrist-camera TOKENS (VLM L21) peak at +0.175 (real R² 0.1391) in [+3.2,+4.8) s.
